name: Mister Download Manager
cost: Free (GPL-3.0), no ads, no trial, no sign-up
works_with: Windows 10 and 11, Linux, and macOS (experimental). Browser extension for Firefox and Chromium browsers
short: A free open source download manager in Rust that splits files into parts, resumes broken downloads and catches them from your browser.
what: Mister Download Manager (MDM) is a clean-room download manager written in Rust, laid out like IDM. It fetches parts of a file at once, resumes after a crash or dropped connection, and has queues, a scheduler and a link grabber. It also handles videos on web pages, image galleries through gallery-dl, and torrents and magnet links. A command-line tool, a local API and an MCP server let scripts and AI assistants manage downloads.
who: Anyone who downloads big files often, and IDM users who want a free option with the same layout. Mac users should know the macOS builds have not been tried on a Mac by the team yet.
needs: Windows 10 or 11, a recent Linux (tested on Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12 and Fedora), or a Mac for the experimental builds
Firefox or a Chromium browser if you want the extension

steps.title: Download the installer
steps.text: On the latest release page, pick `...-setup.exe` if you are not sure. It installs MDM, connects it to your browser and asks your language. There is also a portable ZIP for a USB stick.

steps.title: Or install with WinGet
steps.text: The first line installs MDM and the second updates it.
steps.code:
winget install AhmedNefzaoui.MisterDownloadManager
winget upgrade AhmedNefzaoui.MisterDownloadManager

steps.title: On Linux
steps.text: Use the `.deb` for Ubuntu, Debian, Mint and Pop!_OS, the `.rpm` for Fedora, openSUSE and RHEL, or the AppImage on any Linux.

steps.title: Add the browser extension
steps.text: Get it from Firefox Add-ons or the Chrome Web Store. The Chrome Web Store version also works in Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and Helium.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Follow the README's guide to your first download, then try catching a download from your browser with the extension.

watch: Windows may say "Windows protected your PC" the first time, because this early version is not code-signed yet.
On Linux, screen readers do not read its windows yet and Flatpak browsers cannot reach it.
The macOS builds are marked experimental.
The MCP server lets an AI assistant list, add, pause and remove your downloads.
